doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Baton Rouge, first New York trip, the road years
title: First trip to New York in 1951: Birdland and Miles Davis
summary: Staying with his cousin Mariana Staton, he heard Miles at Birdland but was uncomfortable and did not sit in.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Also, in the summer of 1951, you went to New York for the first time. You made your first...
Oh, yeah.
Mmm-hmm.

You were thinking about going to NYU, which, had you done so, you would have entered with Wayne Shorter, because he entered NYU right at that time. But in any event, you stayed with your cousin, Mariana Staton, who lived on Park Avenue and 96th Street, and you spent some time there, but you weren’t comfortable in New York at that time.
No. I went back to... I thought about southern colleges, with the trees and everything, and the... Well, southern colleges, you know...
The gracious living.
Yeah. Ok.
Or some believe so. But you were a bebop devotee by this time.
Yes.

Here you are in New York, it’s 1951, and there’s Birdland, and bebop is somewhat diminished from what it had been a year or two before... But did you go to hear music? Did you explore the scene at all that summer?

Oh, yeah. I went to hear music. I went to Birdland, and I remember hearing Miles Davis there. He was working weekends, one night a week, with a band that was later...it was not his band, you know... When I went back to New York, I heard he had progressed to the level of an entertainer...
A leader. He improved.
Yes. He was a leader, and he worked at the Village Vanguard opposite Al and Zoot...
Well, these are people with whom you’d be playing with five or six years. They’d be hiring you.
Yeah.
Did you meet any of the people you‘d subsequently on that first trip to New York?
No. Not at the moment. I met them... I met Frank Isola at the 34th Street loft. We used to go there and play.
This is when you moved to New York for good.
Yes.
Did you ever sit in with people during this first trip to New York? Did you go to jam sessions?
No. No, I didn’t sit in.
That first time you went, you didn’t.
No.
I think maybe in ‘51, I didn’t go with you. Or else it was for a very short... I remember Mariana’s apartment, but I don’t think I stayed there.
No. You stayed on 60th Street, at ....(?—35:47)....
Oh, yeah.
